newsitem.title: FRANCE: Waigel-EMU stability council should be informal.
newsitem.headline: Waigel-EMU stability council should be informal.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday he would approve of an informally structured stability council to monitor the euro-currency area after the start of monetary union, which is planned for 1999.

"Like (French Finance Minister) Arthuis, I consider an informal forum to be a sensible idea. We agree that this should be an informal forum ... like the G7," Waigel said after a Franco-German economic summit meeting.
Waigel said the forum should allow an informal exchange of ideas. "It is clear that the independence of the European Central Bank would not be affected in the least," he said.
Waigel also said that Germany was making every effort to meet the Maastricht criteria on budget deficits and said the convergence criteria in the treaty would have to be strictly interpreted.

The level of convergence between potential participants in monetary union was decisive for the euro project's timetable, Waigel said. Also, the timing of the choice of who would participate from the start would take into account the French elections.

Waigel dismissed speculation of what might happen should Germany and France fail to qualify for monetary union, as has been widely rumoured given their sluggish economies and persistently high unemployment rates.
"We now have a chance to use our growth-oriented policies to achieve our goal," Waigel said.
Talk of alternatives to the euro "are not productive and not necessary," he said.
Waigel also emphasised the close co-operation between France and Germany, which he said was important for all EU states, but was not, he said, meant to exclude any other country.
